minutes.headline: Library trustees approved Feb 18 minutes as amended and heard the director's report; no budget votes, reopening and strategic plan updates.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Library Board of Trustees met remotely. They approved the February minutes after capitalization edits, heard the director's FY21 budget status, CW MARS membership fee changes, and a long discussion of library reopening, browsing hours and curbside service. They also got updates on the strategic plan survey, the trustee handbook and bylaws, and the Friends of the Library, then adjourned by roll call.

votes.motion: Accept the February 18 minutes as amended
votes.outcome: passed; roll call yes from Laura, Bob, Richard, Kathleen, Donna, Maya (aye added later)
passed; all members yes on roll call

budget_items.what_was_said: About three quarters through the year with a share expended; salaries low due to a vacancy and some utility bills just paid.
CW MARS voted a reduced fee for small libraries; Lunenburg is moving to full membership over about three years, so assessments will rise.
The E-rate rising in FY23 will partly mitigate the membership assessment increase; the CW MARS budget line request was raised, and state aid has supplemented it.
None of the contractual money has been spent; the facilitator has not yet invoiced.
The Friends increased budget lines for virtual programs and program supplies; also paid for security cameras and Beanstack.
Bid request is being finalized by the architect and will go out soon through DPW.

decisions.decision: Trustees to read chapter two of the trustee handbook before next meeting and discuss chapters one and two.
Bylaws work to be added to the FY22 agenda; Laura to work on preparing bylaws with help from others.
Director to talk to the town manager about starting the search to fill the staff vacancy.

what_happened.line: Library trustees approved the February 18 minutes as amended after capitalization edits, then adjourned by roll call; no budget votes were taken.
The director said Lunenburg is moving to full CW MARS membership over several years, so the library's assessment will rise; an E-rate offset will partly cushion it.
Trustees spent a long stretch on reopening, browsing hours, curbside service and a staff vacancy; the director will ask the town manager about starting the search to fill it.
The strategic plan subcommittee reported that none of the consultant contract money has been spent, because the facilitator has not yet invoiced.
Trustees will read chapter two of the handbook before the next meeting, and bylaws work was added to the FY22 agenda.

why_it_matters: The CW MARS membership change is a rising library assessment that will show up in future library budget requests, which residents fund through the town budget, mostly taxes.
Reopening hours and curbside service decide when residents can use the building, and filling the vacancy bears on staffing for those hours.
watch_next: Trustees' next meeting: chapter two of the handbook to be read beforehand, with chapters one and two discussed.
The recarpeting bid request, which the architect is finalizing to go out through DPW.
